examples: I watch television in the evening.
There is a television in the living room.
I turn off the TV and sleep.
nuance: 텔레비전 is the full loanword for a television, and in casual speech people shorten it to 티비.
mistakes: Saying 텔레비전이 봐요 instead of 텔레비전을 봐요 when you watch it.

usage: I put it in the washer
examples: I run the washing machine on weekends.
I put clothes in the washing machine.
nuance: 세탁기 is the machine that washes clothes, while the verb 돌리다 means to run or operate it.
mistakes: Saying 세탁기를 해요 instead of 세탁기를 돌려요 to run it.

examples: I run the vacuum in the morning.
I clean the room with the vacuum.
I want to buy a new vacuum.
nuance: 청소기 is short for 진공청소기, the machine you use to clean floors and carpets at home.
mistakes: Using 에 instead of 으로 when the vacuum is the means of cleaning.

examples: It is hot so I turn on the air conditioner.
At night I turn off the air conditioner.
There is an air conditioner in the room.
nuance: 에어컨 is the loanword for an air conditioner, and you use 켜다 and 끄다 to turn it on and off.
mistakes: Saying 에어컨을 열어요 instead of 에어컨을 켜요 to turn it on.

examples: I turn on the fan in summer.
I sit in front of the fan.
nuance: 선풍기 is an electric fan that moves air, which is cheaper to run than an 에어컨.
mistakes: Saying 선풍기를 열어요 instead of 선풍기를 켜요 to switch it on.

usage: I put it in the fridge
examples: There is a refrigerator in the kitchen.
I put milk in the refrigerator.
I open the fridge and take out water.
nuance: 냉장고 keeps food cold, and the freezer part inside it is called the 냉동실.
mistakes: Saying 냉장고에서 넣어요 instead of 냉장고에 넣어요 for putting food in.

usage: I heat it in the microwave
I put it in the microwave
examples: I heat rice in the microwave.
I put food in the microwave.
There is a microwave in the kitchen.
nuance: 전자레인지 is the appliance that heats food fast, and people often shorten it to 레인지.
mistakes: Using 에 instead of 으로 when the microwave is the means of heating.

examples: There is a sofa in the living room.
I watch television on the sofa.
nuance: 소파 is a Western style couch for the living room, and a long one is a 긴 소파.
mistakes: Saying 소파에서 앉아요 instead of 소파에 앉아요 for sitting down.

usage: I put it in the wardrobe
examples: There is a wardrobe in the room.
I put clothes in the wardrobe.
I open the wardrobe and take out a coat.
nuance: 옷장 is a closet for storing clothes, while a chest of drawers is usually called a 서랍장.
mistakes: Saying 옷장에서 넣어요 instead of 옷장에 넣어요 for storing clothes.

usage: I put it in the drawer
examples: I open the drawer and take out socks.
I put the key in the drawer.
There is paper inside the drawer.
nuance: 서랍 is a single sliding drawer, and a unit with many drawers is called a 서랍장.
mistakes: Saying 서랍이 열어요 instead of 서랍을 열어요 when you open it.

examples: I draw the curtains at night.
I open the curtains in the morning.
There is a curtain on the window.
nuance: 커튼 is a fabric window cover, and the verb 치다 means to draw or close it across the window.
mistakes: Saying 커튼을 해요 instead of 커튼을 쳐요 to draw them.

usage: I put it on the shelf
examples: There is a bookshelf in the room.
I put books on the bookshelf.
There is a chair next to the bookshelf.
nuance: 책장 is a shelf for storing books, and a closed bookcase with doors is a 책꽂이 alternative.
mistakes: Saying 책장에서 꽂아요 instead of 책장에 꽂아요 for shelving books.
